score_rationale: Solid willingness-to-pay evidence from healthcare staffing agencies and travel nursing companies who pay $0.10–$0.50 per nurse contact for recruitment lists. The Texas Board of Nursing (BON) provides a free, publicly-searchable online verification tool and bulk data via public records request. Texas has 450,000+ active RN and LPN licenses — the second-largest nurse population in the US after California. Healthcare recruiters, continuing education vendors, malpractice insurers, and career fair organizers all actively purchase nurse contact lists. No affordable flat-file product exists on Gumroad or low-cost marketplaces. Engineering lift is moderate — requires web scraping or FOIA request, then deduplication and formatting. Zero PII concerns if limited to professional license data (name, license number, license type, issue date, expiration, status, city). Score held at 7 (not 8) because data acquisition requires scraping or public records request rather than direct CSV download, adding modest friction.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all active Registered Nurse (RN) and Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN) licenses in Texas, extracted from the Texas Board of Nursing public license verification database — freely accessible (with rate limiting) at bon.texas.gov or obtainable via Texas Public Information Act request. Each record includes the nurse's full name, license number, license type (RN, LVN), original issue date, current expiration date, license status (active, inactive, retired, suspended), city of record (no street address to avoid PII concerns), and any public disciplinary actions or restrictions. Texas is the second-largest nursing workforce in the US with approximately 450,000+ active RN and LVN licenses as of 2025. Healthcare staffing agencies (Cross Country Nurses, Aya Healthcare, AMN Healthcare, Fastaff) and travel nursing companies pay list brokers $0.10–$0.50 per contact for nurse recruitment data. Nursing continuing education (CE) providers, malpractice insurance brokers, career fair organizers, and healthcare software vendors targeting individual nurses all represent additional buyer segments. A one-time $79 CSV targets healthcare recruiters building cold-call lists, CE vendors marketing license renewal courses, and career platforms (Nurse.com, Incredible Health) enriching their user databases.

audience.who: Healthcare staffing and travel nursing agencies (AMN Healthcare, Cross Country Nurses, Aya Healthcare, Fastaff, Medical Solutions, Nomad Health, plus 2,000+ regional agencies) building recruitment prospect lists of RNs and LVNs for travel contracts, per diem shifts, and permanent placements; nursing continuing education providers (Wild Iris Medical Education, NetCE, Nurse.com CE, RN.com) marketing Texas-specific license renewal CE courses required every two years; professional liability (malpractice) insurance brokers and carriers (Nurses Service Organization, Proliability, CM&F Group) targeting individual nurses for $100–$500/year professional liability policies; nursing career platforms and job boards (Nurse.com, Indeed Healthcare, Incredible Health, Vivian Health) enriching their databases with verified RN/LVN contacts for email recruitment campaigns; nursing school recruiters and BSN/MSN completion program directors (Western Governors University, Capella, Chamberlain University) targeting LVNs for RN bridge programs and RNs for BSN or MSN degree completion; healthcare career fair organizers and nursing conference planners building invite lists for regional nursing summits and job fairs.

data_wanted: Texas Board of Nursing (BON) license verification database — accessible via https://vo.bon.texas.gov/lookup/ (web portal with rate-limited lookups) or bulk extract via Texas Public Information Act request to bon.texas.gov. Key fields per license: license number (7-digit numeric ID), full name (first, middle initial, last), license type (RN=Registered Nurse, LVN=Licensed Vocational Nurse, APRN=Advanced Practice Registered Nurse), license status (Active, Inactive, Retired, Suspended, Revoked, Expired), original issue date, current expiration date (licenses renew every 2 years on the nurse's birthday), city and state of record (street address excluded to avoid PII), and any public disciplinary actions (board orders, consent agreements, restrictions, or probation — these are public record per Texas Occupations Code). Scope to active RN and LVN licenses only (exclude APRN, retired, and suspended unless buyer specifically wants disciplinary action leads). Approximately 350,000 active RNs and 100,000 active LVNs in Texas as of 2025. Target output: 450,000 rows, one per active license, with all public metadata. Data can be acquired via web scraping (with respectful rate limiting and User-Agent identification per BON terms of use) or via formal Texas Public Information Act request (typically fulfilled within 10 business days as a CSV or Excel file).

willingness_to_pay.signal: Four distinct buyer segments with validated purchasing behavior. (1) Healthcare staffing agencies: travel nursing and per diem staffing companies pay list brokers $0.10–$0.50 per nurse contact for recruitment data; a $79 CSV of 450,000 Texas RNs/LVNs delivers contacts at $0.00018 each — 500× cheaper than current broker rates, making it a trivial acquisition cost against the $1,500–$3,000 commission per placed travel nurse. (2) Nursing CE providers: continuing education vendors routinely pay $0.05–$0.20 per contact for targeted email lists; a single $49 course sale (typical CE course price for 10–20 contact hours) from a 450K email list yields instant ROI. (3) Malpractice insurers: professional liability carriers pay $50–$200 per policy sold; targeting 450K individual nurses with a $79 list investment is negligible against a $100–$500 annual premium on even a 0.5% conversion rate (2,250 policies = $225K–$1.125M in premium). (4) Nursing career platforms: Indeed Healthcare, Incredible Health, and Vivian Health spend millions on nurse acquisition via paid ads; a $79 CSV for organic email outreach is a rounding error. The absence of any flat-file competitor on Gumroad or comparable marketplaces (all competitors are annual subscription services like NursingLicenseMap or bundled into $10K+ healthcare data platforms) creates an open niche.
